name: Performance testing
note: Questions authored by Claude as practice material. Not sourced from your own notes or any official exam. Verify anything you doubt against the docs.

questions.q: What does p95 response time mean?
options: 95% of requests were at or below this time
questions.why: It is a percentile, not an average.

options: Load: expected traffic; stress: beyond capacity to find the breaking point
Load: one user; stress: two users

questions.why: Latency is time per request; throughput is volume per time.

questions.q: In k6, how do you make a run fail automatically when p95 is too slow?
Why record a baseline before changes?
options: So later results can be compared against a known reference
questions.why: Without a baseline you cannot tell if performance regressed.

options: A simulated concurrent user in a load test
questions.why: VUs run the script in parallel.

questions.q: What is the purpose of ramp-up?
options: To increase load gradually so the system is not hit instantly
questions.why: It makes problems easier to attribute.

options: A few very slow requests barely move the mean but hurt real users
questions.why: Look at percentiles like p95 and p99.

questions.q: Why should the test environment resemble production?
options: Results from very different hardware or data do not predict production
questions.why: Data size and config affect performance.

questions.q: What does a soak test look for?
options: Problems that appear over long periods such as memory leaks
questions.why: It runs moderate load for hours.

questions.q: How do you find the bottleneck during a load test?
options: Correlate response times with server metrics such as CPU, memory, database and connection pools
questions.why: Client numbers show the symptom; server metrics show the cause.

options: A load generator that waits for a slow response and so under-records the latency users would have seen
questions.why: It can make tail latencies look better than they are.
